entries.name: Kent Ford

sources.title: Oregon Encyclopedia: Black Panther Party in Portland
sources.locator: June 1969 arrest and jailing preceding the Portland chapter.

sources.title: Martha Gies, Radical Treatment, Reed Magazine, December 2009
sources.locator: Account of Ford at Rocky Butte Jail and subsequent bail release.

sources.title: The Militant, July 4, 1969
sources.locator: Portland report distinguishes June 14 initial arrest and June 18 rearrest.

entries.notes: Month precision accommodates the initial arrest and rearrest; no exact release date or calculated custody duration is asserted. Existing sentence and biography are preserved.

entries.name: Larry Gossett

sources.title: Tikia Gilbert, The Franklin High School Sit-in, University of Washington
sources.locator: The Hearing, The Trial, and Sentencing sections; contemporary newspaper citations in footnotes 18, 23-25.

entries.notes: The existing March 29 arrest date is preserved despite the source placing arrest on April 4. Separate April and July custody episodes are not combined into an invented continuous interval.

entries.name: Larry Little
entries.match_charges: Accessory after the fact (the January 1971 Winston-Salem "meat-truck" frame-up of the NCCF)

fields.convicted: Yes — no-contest plea to misdemeanor larceny
fields.sentence: Six months in jail, suspended for two years, following a no-contest plea to misdemeanor larceny.

sources.title: Benjamin R. Friedman, Picking Up Where Robert F. Williams Left Off, in Comrades (2007)
sources.locator: Printed pages 69 and 73: January 19, 1971 arrest, later misdemeanor disposition and suspended sentence.

sources.title: FBI Vault, Black Panther Party Part 34
sources.locator: PDF pages 47 (printed 6) and 60 (printed 4), visually checked: March 19, 1973 plea disposition, Copeland, six months suspended for two years.

sources.title: State v. Cornell, 281 N.C. 20, 187 S.E.2d 768 (April 12, 1972)
sources.locator: Appeal concerning the bills of indictment against Cornell and Little.

entries.notes: The original felony charge is preserved; the newly filled disposition describes the reduced misdemeanor. A suspended sentence is not six months actually served. No duration or release date is added. Fuller’s 12 pretrial days and 90-day sentence do not belong to Little. Little’s separate 1970 disorderly-conduct case is outside this existing-case update.

entries.name: Scott Camil
entries.match_charges: Conspiracy to incite a riot at the 1972 Republican National Convention

sources.title: The Texas Observer, The VVAW is not on trial, September 21, 1973
sources.locator: Printed/PDF page 5, visually checked: grand-jury proceedings, trial judge, and prosecutor in the Gainesville Eight case.

entries.notes: Existing arrest date, acquittal, sentence text and court institution remain unchanged. An acquittal date alone does not establish a release from physical custody.

entries.name: Connie Matthews
entries.match_charges: No personal criminal charges — fled the U.S. as a political fugitive

sources.title: TIME, Radicals: The Divided Panthers, February 22, 1971
sources.locator: Contemporary report of Matthews disappearing with Tabor and Moore during February; later historical accounts establish their arrival in Algeria.

sources.title: The Black Panther Party’s Publishing Strategies and the Financial Underpinnings of Activism, 1968–1975, The Historical Journal
sources.locator: Matthews, Tabor and Moore disappeared and resurfaced in Algeria weeks later; March 1971 expulsion announcement.

sources.title: Connie Matthews biography (secondary corroboration)
sources.locator: Departure in February 1971 and subsequent appearance in Algeria.

entries.notes: Month precision, corroborating the departure already described in her unchanged biography. Exile is not imprisonment. Tabor’s Panther 21 charges and trial personnel are not assigned to Matthews.

entries.name: Mabel Williams
entries.match_charges: Fled the United States with Robert F.

sources.title: Sue Sturgis, Remembering Southern Black freedom fighter Mabel Williams, Facing South, April 2014
sources.locator: Mabel returned to the United States in September 1969; Robert followed and was arrested.

entries.notes: Month precision only. Existing exile start, charges and sentence are preserved. Robert’s arrest on return is not attributed to Mabel; no custody dates are added.
